Starving horses

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A top equestrian judges horses confiscated after they were allegedly found starving abandoned and neglected.

Summary:
It all started with a photo on facebook that went viral of a starving and neglected stallion standing dejected in a stable without bedding or anything to eat. To the horror of the horse community this horse belonged to one of the country's leading showing judges.

Now showing is like a beauty pageant - except you want your horses to be as fat and round and shiny as possible with no blemishes - essentially a picture of equine perfection. The 14 horses confiscated by Wetnose were anything but. Thin, some emaciated and in need of a farrier and dentist.

Further information:
All 14 horses were confiscated while judge Carol Dollery was at the Showing Nationals with 2 of her horses that were in peak condition - she fed them for the show ring but neglected the rest who were not seen by the public.


Since the incident many people have come forward to recount how Carol has neglected her horses for nearly 2 decades and how she has left unpaid bills at vets and stable yards all over Gauteng.

Press Release:


Starving Horses
When a photograph of an emaciated and dejected horse standing in a stable with no bedding nor food went viral among South Africa's passionate horse community, it emerged that the horse was in fact a stallion belonging to one of the country’s most respected equestrian judges. Carte Blanche exposes the shocking condition of horses confiscated from the premises and a history of alleged abuse.


Script:


Script – Starving Horses


VO: 18”

They take care to ensure they are smartly and correctly attired befitting the rules of the sport. Hours are spent on the finer details of turning out a horse: grooming, plaiting manes, cleaning and polishing hooves and even stray hairs are taken care of with painstaking care.

Devi link
Essentially it’s the beauty pageant of the horse world…in perfect condition.






Groom taking out manure VO: 25

The woman who blew the whistle is Marion Clough. At the end of October Carol moved her horses to Marions yard where she rented stables and was meant to care for them herself.

Marion:
…three days this carried on for.

VO: 8”
Marion says she was shocked by the condition of Carol’s horses.

Marion:
Filthy, absolutely skinny

VO: 11”
Then to Marion’s horror Carol took two of her horses which she kept in show condition to the showing national championships and left the rest in the stables with no food or bedding.

statement Marion:
She promised me that they would do a delivery.

VO: Bern you have said we asked her for an interview etc later in script but should it not come here?
We approached Carol for an interview but she declined in light of pending legal action. Instead in a statement she said she did leave 44 bales of hay and arranged with a feed store to deliver food. They never arrived and so when the horses ran out of food she organized for a friend to drop some off. When the friend arrived she was so shocked by the horses condition that she convinced Marion to call in Wetnose inspector Tarryn Smith.

Tarryn:
I was horrified….

Devi link
…decision was made to move the horses.

If we hadn’t have taken them standing in their stables with no food.

Of the 14 horses confiscated this 20 year old stallion was in the worst condition. We asked nutritionist Christelle King to body score him for us out of 5.

Christelle:
21:50 did not happen overnight -…malnutrition over a period of time.

His face was sunken and he was about 200kg’s underweight.

Christelle:
The neck has also …no fat deposit here at all.

VO: 7”
His ribs and spine were clearly protruding.

His hip bones were prominent and his rump clearly visible.

…because that’s how skinny this poor horse is.

VO: 3”

Christelle
There’s no shape to the hoof at all.

Kim:
The young horse that we did down there had a hip problem, wither problems, very malnourished.

Kim:
I found quite a few horses that ….inflammation and pain.

The old stallion’s teeth were in a shocking condition.

Could lose Christelle:
…I’m sorry my boy.

VO: 3”
For Christelle these teeth tell a story.

I definitely think he was depressed… because he was hungry – chewing on…must have been so frustrated…

She used to steal food for the horses…didn’t do anything about it.

****NO response to stealing from him?

…it luckily survived.

Tracey:
When the inspector…swept through the yard.

VO: 3

Devi: She’s written a statement and everyone else is at fault – she takes no responsibility.

34:55…hoarder…I don’t know.

…in that condition.

Wessel:

I sincerely hope that they step up and …nothing has been done.

VO: 5”
When Carol returned from the national championships came to see .

Tarryn:
She signed several of them over to us….until the investigation is over.

But three weeks later she contested the confiscation on the basis that she never abandoned them and had left them in the care of a groom.

Link

Outcome of high court application

Tarryn/Carol
How they feel about the outcome…vindicated? Upset whatever

VO: 12”

Tracey:
It takes courage to stand up but it …against them in the ring.

Roger:
Someone should have done something years ago….

VO:

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A top equestrian judges horses confiscated after they were allegedly found starving abandoned and neglected.
metadata.Summary: It all started with a photo on facebook that went viral of a starving and neglected stallion standing dejected in a stable without bedding or anything to eat. To the horror of the horse community this horse belonged to one of the country's leading showing judges. Now showing is like a beauty pageant - except you want your horses to be as fat and round and shiny as possible with no blemishes - essentially a picture of equine perfection. The 14 horses confiscated by Wetnose were anything but. Thin, some emaciated and in need of a farrier and dentist.
metadata.Further information: All 14 horses were confiscated while judge Carol Dollery was at the Showing Nationals with 2 of her horses that were in peak condition - she fed them for the show ring but neglected the rest who were not seen by the public. Since the incident many people have come forward to recount how Carol has neglected her horses for nearly 2 decades and how she has left unpaid bills at vets and stable yards all over Gauteng.
